checks.note: batch running; figures are rebuilt when it ends

notes: F4 storm catalogue and batch: N = 47 catalogue storms (interim weights), 1000 of 1000 years covered. Depth frequency is empirical (catalogue.depth_at, RainyDay's rank convention), one storm per synthetic year; the largest-rain storm of a year is taken as its worst flood. Grid depth: calibration.run_depth (src/flood_lab/hazard/calibration.py): peak water level less the model terrain at each 5 m cell's centre 1 m pixel, floored at 0, the definition the drainage allowance was calibrated and FH8 tested on; not read (NaN) where calibration.Frame leaves a cell out: centre pixel in a building footprint, any pixel in a filled pit, centre pixel on mapped water, lowest level below the start water level (CH-16). Whole square, not only the study area. Asset depths: at_assets (1 m pixels; substation lead measure, building wall band). Figures made before the batch completes are rebuilt afterwards (requirements §15).

domain.png: 3-hour ratio map (smoothed mean annual maximum over the study area's, AORC 2002-2025) over the download window, domain B, the study box and the 960 storms of the chosen catalogue, each at the centre of the box-sized window of its largest 3-hour rain (RainyDay's storm location).

rainfall_frequency.png: 3-hour annual maximum rainfall at the study box: the chosen catalogue (960 storms, M = 1000, T = M / rank), the 240- and 480-storm sensitivities, Atlas 14 AMS 3-hr with its 90% band, and AORC observed box maxima at Weibull plotting positions T = (n + 1) / i. Below the band at 2-10 y: fail, accepted (CH-19).

depth_strip.png: Per-cell depth at 10, 100 and 500 years from the catalogue (N = 47 catalogue storms (interim weights), 1000 of 1000 years covered) beside the 1-hour and 3-hour Atlas 14 design storms of the same return periods.

buildings_wet.png: Buildings of the study area wet at the wall (0.05 m, 0.3 m) at 100 years: the catalogue (N = 47 catalogue storms (interim weights), 1000 of 1000 years covered; each building's own curve at AEP 0.01) against each design storm; beside it every design storm with the 5 m cells it wets. Shaded: storms that wet no 5 m cell or whose rain does not exceed the 30 mm/h constant loss rate; since CH-20 and CH-21 (ground never below a cell's lowest sub-grid level) they wet no cell and no building, where before they showed about 2,900 buildings.
wet_runs.png: Number of catalogue runs wetting each read 5 m cell (N = 47 catalogue storms (interim weights), 1000 of 1000 years covered).
progress.png: Catalogue runs finished per stratum; solver wall time and water-balance residual per finished run (catalogue and design).
Other folders in the runs folder, not read: cat_r0023.
